deep.reconstruction:
Euler's notation. For a fixed weight N = m+n, q^μ denotes the 'singular series' Σ_{x≥1} (1 + 1/2^{N-μ} + … + 1/x^{N-μ}) / x^μ. In modern terms this is the double sum S(μ, N-μ) = ζ(μ, N-μ) + ζ(N), with the diagonal term included. For 2 ≤ μ ≤ N-2, p^μ denotes the product ζ(μ)ζ(N-μ), and p^N denotes ζ(N).

The 'first method' gives the reflection formula q^μ + q^{N-μ} = p^μ + p^N. The second and third methods give further linear relations; these are the partial-fraction / Goldbach-type relations, including the sum relation Σ_{j=2}^{N-1} q^j = (N-1)p^N and the alternating relation Σ (-1)^j q^j = ½p^N. Euler then solves the resulting linear system order by order.

Order 6 (end of the previous page's system). Result: q^5 = 7/4 ζ(6) - ½ζ(3)^2, q^4 = ζ(3)^2 - ⅓ζ(6), q^3 = ½ζ(3)^2 + ½ζ(6), q^2 = 37/12 ζ(6) - ζ(3)^2. This uses ζ(2)ζ(4) = 7/4 ζ(6), which follows from the even-zeta Bernoulli formulas.

Order 7. The three reflection relations are supplemented by the method-II and method-III relations. Euler finds:
- Σ H_x/x^6 = 4ζ7 - ζ2ζ5 - ζ3ζ4
- Σ H^{(2)}_x/x^5 = -10ζ7 + 5ζ2ζ5 + 2ζ3ζ4
- Σ H^{(3)}_x/x^4 = 18ζ7 - 10ζ2ζ5
- Σ H^{(4)}_x/x^3 = -17ζ7 + 10ζ2ζ5 + ζ3ζ4
- Σ H^{(5)}_x/x^2 = 11ζ7 - 4ζ2ζ5 - 2ζ3ζ4
The system is fully determined, so every weight-7 double sum reduces to zeta values and products.

Order 8. Euler sets up the reflection relations (4 of them), four method-II relations and six method-III relations. On the next page these determine only q^7 = Σ H_x/x^7 = 9/2 ζ8 - ζ2ζ6 - ζ3ζ5 - ½ζ4^2. The rest collapse to a single relation. Euler explicitly notes that the method does not determine everything in weight 8, although it did for weights 5 and 7, and later 9 and 11.

This is the phenomenon now understood as follows: double zeta values of odd weight reduce to products of single zetas, whereas even weight leaves irreducibles such as ζ(5,3) (the parity theorem).
errors: No mathematical errors found in the checked results. I verified the weight-6 values against the modern ζ(4,2) = ζ(3)^2 - 4/3 ζ(6), provided the fractions are read as 1/3 (see transcription corrections).

I verified all five weight-7 values against modern values: S(6,1), S(5,2) = 5ζ2ζ5 + 2ζ3ζ4 - 10ζ7, S(4,3) = 18ζ7 - 10ζ2ζ5, and the others via reflection. I also checked them against the sum, reflection and method-III relations.
The weight-8 method-II relation 3q^2 - q^3 + 3q^4 - q^5 + 3q^6 - q^7 = 8p^8 checks out, using ζ2ζ6 = 5/3 ζ8 and ζ4^2 = 7/6 ζ8.

The third method-II relation in order 7, as transcribed ('4q^3 + 8q^4 - 2q^5 = 6p^7'), is not satisfied by Euler's own final values: it gives 96ζ7 on the left. Either the scan/transcription is misread or it is a misprint. It does not affect the conclusions, since the method-III system alone determines everything.

ideas.what: Closed forms of all weight-7 double Euler sums in terms of ζ(7), ζ(2)ζ(5), ζ(3)ζ(4)
ideas.modern_name: Evaluation of double zeta values / linear Euler sums S_{p,q} of odd weight
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1776); systematic proof for odd weight by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) and later Flajolet–Salvy (1998)
ideas.where_published: E477 itself; discussed in the Opera omnia I.15 and in modern MZV literature (Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst, Flajolet–Salvy)

ideas.what: Sum and alternating-sum relations used as linear constraints (Σ q^j = (N-1)ζ(N), Σ(-1)^j q^j = ½ζ(N))
ideas.modern_name: Sum theorem for double zeta values (Euler/Goldbach); shuffle/stuffle-type linear relations

ideas.what: Observation that the linear system determines all double sums for weights 5, 7, 9, 11 but not for weights 6 (partially) and 8
ideas.modern_name: Parity theorem / irreducibility of even-weight double zetas such as ζ(5,3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Observation credited to Euler; theorem by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn, Tsumura

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of Euler's well-known tabulation of double Euler sums for weights 6–8. These results, and his odd/even-weight observation, are widely cited in the modern multiple-zeta literature and credited to E477. The computations are correct, apart from one apparently misprinted or misread auxiliary relation.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'q^4 = p^3 - ½p^6' should almost certainly read 'q^4 = p^3 - ⅓p^6'. This is consistent with the printed q^2 = p^2 - p^3 + 4/3 p^6 and with the true value ζ(3)^2 - ζ(6)/3.
Last line of the order-6 block: 'q^4 = -½p^6 + p^3' should read 'q^4 = -⅓p^6 + p^3'. This is required by the printed q^2 = 37/12 p^6 - p^3 and the reflection q^2 + q^4 = p^2 + p^6 with p^2 = 7/4 p^6.
Order 7, method II, third line '4q^3 + 8q^4 - 2q^5 = 6p^7' is inconsistent with the results. It is possibly a misreading of the scan or an original misprint; check the image.
Order 8, method III, fourth line: the asterisk marks the missing q^3 term (coefficient 0), as Euler prints it.
